documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

33 y/o woman here to establish. Has not had a regular doctor in years -- no insurance until she picked up MassHealth last month. Main reason she came in now: about six months of being thirsty all the time, up several times a night to urinate, and losing weight without trying. Clothes looser. Some fatigue. No vomiting, no abdominal pain, no shortness of breath. Drinking a lot of water and some juice.

PMH
- Hypertension, found during a hospital stay in 2020. Was sent home on lisinopril 10 and metoprolol succinate 50. Ran out a few months ago and never got them refilled.
- Kidney cancer: left kidney removed in 2020 at an outside hospital (clear cell RCC per her). Never had follow-up after.
- Bipolar I disorder, diagnosed years ago. Not on anything now. Says mood has been OK lately. Would like to get back in with psychiatry now that she has coverage.

PSH: left radical nephrectomy 2020.
Meds: none currently.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother has type 2 diabetes.
SH: part-time administrative assistant. Never smoked. Drinks socially, a drink or two a month. Lives in Holyoke.

ROS: as above. No chest pain, no vision change, no dysuria.

EXAM
BP 130/85. BMI 22. Thin, looks dry -- dry mucous membranes, otherwise in no distress. Alert, conversant.
Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed left flank incision. No edema. Skin without rash.

IN-OFFICE TESTS
Fingerstick glucose 380 (random).
POC A1c 11.2%.
Urine dip: glucose 3+, ketones 1+.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Diabetes mellitus, new, symptomatic -- type 2. Mother with T2DM. Small ketones on dip but she is eating and drinking, no vomiting, looks dry but not sick. BMP sent today to make sure bicarb and gap are OK; will call her this afternoon. Start metformin 500 mg BID with meals, will titrate in two weeks. Push water, cut out juice and soda. Glucometer prescribed, check fasting and before supper. Diabetes education referral. Reviewed ED precautions: vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion, trouble breathing.
2. Hypertension -- 130/85 off meds. Restart her prior lisinopril 10 daily and metoprolol succinate 50 daily. BMP today, recheck at next visit.
3. History of RCC s/p left nephrectomy, solitary right kidney -- will request the hospital records.
4. Bipolar I -- stable by her report, PHQ-9 5. Referral to psychiatry.
5. Health maintenance -- HIV and hep C screens today with consent. TSH, CBC.

Follow up 2 weeks (video OK).

documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside Gynecology -- Consultation Letter
Date of service: 09/05/2022

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Ms. Strong, a 33-year-old G0, for evaluation of irregular cycles and difficulty conceiving.

HISTORY: Over the last six months her cycles have lengthened and become unpredictable, now every 45 to 60 days, with heavy flow each time. She and her partner have been attempting conception for six months. She was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes by your office and is on metformin.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, bipolar I disorder, clear cell renal cell carcinoma s/p left radical nephrectomy (age 31).
MEDICATIONS: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
FAMILY HISTORY: Father -- Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome. Mother -- type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Maternal uncle -- bipolar disorder.
SOCIAL: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks monthly; part-time administrative assistant.

EXAM: BP 135/85. Central adiposity. Acanthosis nigricans at the posterior neck and axillae. Hirsutism of the chin and lower abdomen. Thyroid not enlarged. Pelvic exam: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, uterus normal size, no adnexal masses.

LABS (drawn today): fasting glucose 126 mg/dL; hemoglobin A1c 7.2%; total testosterone 45 ng/dL (reference 8-60); SHBG low at 14 nmol/L; estrone elevated at 262 pg/mL.

IMPRESSION: Oligomenorrhea with heavy bleeding, hirsutism and acanthosis in the setting of insulin resistance -- consistent with polycystic ovary syndrome. Testosterone within range; low SHBG and elevated estrone fit the picture.

PLAN: Continue metformin per your office. Menstrual calendar. Follow up with us as needed.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

- MRI brain and cervical/thoracic spine with and without contrast
- Abdominal ultrasound (solitary R kidney, never had post-op imaging)

conditions.label: Neoplasm of uncertain behavior of right kidney

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound abdomen, complete.
INDICATION: History of renal cell carcinoma, status post left nephrectomy.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct 3 mm. Pancreas partially obscured by bowel gas; visualized portions unremarkable. Spleen 9.8 cm. Left kidney surgically absent; no mass in the left nephrectomy bed. Right kidney 11.9 cm with normal cortical thickness. Multiple simple cysts in the right kidney, the largest 1.4 cm in the upper pole. In the interpolar region there is a 2.0 x 1.8 cm solid, mildly hypoechoic mass with internal vascularity. No hydronephrosis or stone. Aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion:
1. Solid 2.0 cm mass in the solitary right kidney, suspicious for neoplasm; MRI recommended.
2. Multiple simple right renal cysts.
3. Postsurgical absence of the left kidney.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: MRI brain without and with IV gadolinium.
INDICATION: Headaches, visual disturbance, family history of VHL.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: In the left cerebellar hemisphere there is a 1.1 cm avidly enhancing nodule abutting the pial surface. A second 0.6 cm enhancing nodule is present in the inferior vermis. No associated cyst. No surrounding edema. Fourth ventricle normal in size; no hydrocephalus. Supratentorial brain normal. No acute infarct or hemorrhage on diffusion and susceptibility imaging. Orbits and globes grossly normal on this exam. Paranasal sinuses clear.
reports.conclusion: Two enhancing cerebellar nodules (left hemisphere 1.1 cm, vermis 0.6 cm) consistent with hemangioblastomas in the setting of suspected VHL. No hydrocephalus.

reports.study: MRI cervical and thoracic spine with and without contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: MRI cervical and thoracic spine without and with IV gadolinium.
INDICATION: Suspected VHL, screening for spinal hemangioblastoma.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Small intramedullary enhancing nodules at C4 (0.4 cm) and T8 (0.5 cm), dorsally located, without syrinx or cord expansion. Remainder of the cord normal in signal and caliber. Vertebral body heights and alignment preserved. No significant disc herniation or canal stenosis.
reports.conclusion: Two small intramedullary enhancing nodules at C4 and T8 consistent with hemangioblastomas. No syrinx.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Results visit. Spent most of the visit going through findings with her; she had already read the reports on the portal and came with questions.

Imaging:
- MRI brain: two cerebellar hemangioblastomas (L hemisphere 1.1 cm, vermis 0.6 cm), no hydrocephalus.
- MRI C/T spine: small intramedullary hemangioblastomas at C4 and T8, no syrinx.
- US abdomen: 2.0 cm solid mass in the remaining (right) kidney plus multiple simple cysts.
Labs: plasma free normetanephrine 476 (ref <148), metanephrine normal 42. Hgb 13.2, Hct 39.8, Ca 9.8.
Fundi 12/5: left retinal angiomas.

Headaches unchanged, no new neuro symptoms. Blurry spells in L eye continue occasionally.

Exam: vitals as charted. Neuro nonfocal, gait normal.

ASSESSMENT
Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome -- clinical diagnosis: father affected, plus her own clear cell RCC, CNS hemangioblastomas and retinal angiomas. Elevated normetanephrine raises concern for a catecholamine-secreting tumor.

PLAN
- Neurology for the hemangioblastomas
- Urology for the solid right renal mass in a solitary kidney
- Endocrinology for the elevated normetanephrine (and her diabetes)
- Ophthalmology referral already placed 12/5
- Talked about what VHL means for her brother and other relatives; she will let her family know.
- HTN: 142/90 last time. No change today; endocrinology to weigh in.
- DM: A1c 7.0. Continue metformin.

F/u 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY -- RETINA
Visit 01/24/2023

Re: Susan Strong, DOB 01/06/1989

Thank you for this referral. 34-year-old woman with newly diagnosed Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome and type 2 diabetes, intermittent blurring of the left eye.

Visual acuity: 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal, no APD. IOP 15 / 16. Anterior segments quiet.
Dilated fundus exam:
OD -- normal disc, macula and vessels; no retinal angioma; no diabetic retinopathy.
OS -- two small peripheral retinal capillary hemangioblastomas (angiomas) temporally with dilated feeder vessels, no exudate, no subretinal fluid, macula flat and dry. No diabetic retinopathy.

Impression: VHL-associated retinal angiomas, left eye. No diabetic retinopathy either eye.

Procedure: after consent, laser photocoagulation was applied to both lesions in the left eye. Tolerated well.

Plan: return in one year for dilated exam, sooner for any change in vision. Diabetic eye exam satisfied for this year.

Medications reviewed: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate. Allergies: NKDA.

Retina Service

documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY CONSULTATION -- 02/21/2023

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Strong today. She is a 34-year-old with VHL, s/p left radical nephrectomy in 2020 for clear cell RCC, now with a 2.0 cm solid enhancing lesion in her solitary right kidney on MRI 2/13/23, along with simple cysts.

Allergies: NKDA. Meds: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol.

Exam: well appearing, healed left flank incision, no CVA tenderness.
Creatinine 1.0 on your recent labs.

Assessment: VHL-associated renal tumor, 2.0 cm, solitary kidney.
Plan: For VHL renal tumors we follow with active surveillance and consider nephron-sparing treatment when the largest solid lesion reaches 3 cm. Repeat MRI abdomen in 12 months. Avoid NSAIDs given solitary kidney. She understands and agrees.

Urology

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology -- new consult, 3/14/2023

Reason: CNS hemangioblastomas in newly diagnosed VHL.

Ms. Strong reports intermittent frontal headaches over the past several months, a few days a week, relieved partly by acetaminophen. No vomiting, no gait trouble, no limb weakness or sensory change, no bladder symptoms. Left eye blurring was treated by retina in January.

Exam: alert, fluent. Cranial nerves intact. Strength full, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, toes down. Sensation intact. Finger-nose and heel-shin normal, tandem gait normal.

Imaging reviewed (12/14/22): left cerebellar 1.1 cm and vermian 0.6 cm hemangioblastomas without cyst or hydrocephalus; small C4 and T8 intramedullary lesions without syrinx.

Impression: Asymptomatic-appearing small hemangioblastomas; headaches not localizing and not clearly attributable to the lesions.
Plan: Observation. Repeat MRI brain in 12-18 months, sooner for new headache pattern, imbalance, weakness or numbness. Acetaminophen as needed; limit to a few days a week.

Neurology

34 y/o F. Interval: endocrinology 6/13 -- told she has Cushing syndrome based on exam; dexamethasone test 6/20 was not suppressed (4.1). Endo follow-up in September for ACTH and next steps. Psychiatry finally saw her 5/30 and started olanzapine 10 at night; sleeping better, feels steadier. Gyn dx PCOS last fall; cycles still irregular.

Current meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, metoprolol succ 50, olanzapine 10 qhs.
